body:
In reference to: #36447

Problem:
Whitespace-only messages are unnecessarily rendered.

Solution:
Skip messages containing only whitespace, while preserving empty-message clearing and appended fragments.

comment_data.body: why? i guess kind=empty has a functional purpose to "clear" the message area. what is meant by appended framents?
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -465,6 +465,16 @@ function M.msg_show(kind, content, replace_last, _, append, id, trigger)
     or (kind ~= '' and ui.cfg.msg.targets[kind])
     or ui.cfg.msg.targets.default
 
+  local msg = ''
+  for _, chunk in ipairs(content) do
+    msg = msg .. chunk[2]
+  end
+
+  -- Don't filter empty messages or appended fragments.

comment_data.body:
expect_unchanged is a clumsy way to test things, should be a last resort.

would the test be meaningful if we did something like:


    command('echo "   "')
    command('echo "after space"')
    command('echo "\t\t"')
    command('echo "after tab"')
    command('echo "\n\n"')
    command('echo "after newlines"')
    screen:expect{...}
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -420,6 +420,24 @@ describe('messages2', function()
     ]])
   end)
 
+  it('skips blank messages', function()
+    command('echo "foo"')
+    screen:expect([[
+      ^                                                     |
+      {1:~                                                    }|*12
+      foo                                                  |
+    ]])
+
+    command('echo "   "')
+    screen:expect_unchanged()
+
+    command('echo "\t\t"')
+    screen:expect_unchanged()
+
+    command('echo "\n\n"')
+    screen:expect_unchanged()

comment_data.body:
Yeah, kind=empty has a functional purpose and the elseif condition (a bit further down) handles the case.
Now, I think this existing test case `'properly formatted carriage return messages'` ,should explain what I intended to do: 
```lua
command([[echon "\r" | echon "Hello" | echon " " | echon "World"]])
screen:expect([[
  ^                                                     |
  {1:~                                                    }|*18
  Hello World                                          |
]])
```
Without the `not append` condition, the " " (space) between "Hello" and "World" gets swallowed up.

comment_data.body:
The single final screen:expect() does not work as with separate `command()` calls, the message area can expand between commands, so the intermediate messages aren't reliably represented in one final screen.

got rid of the `expect_unchanged` though.

comment_regular_data.body: Does this trim blank lines at the start/end of messages? I think we should that... probably

> Does this trim blank lines at the start/end of messages? I think we should that... probably

No, it does not currently, and from my understanding it should depend on the user, isn't it? 
Like somebody wants to display 6 spaces or 3 lines before their hello message, do you think this should be altered ??   It does not feel very intuitive tbh, when I do `:echo "      hello"`  , with spaces trimmed off, feels like :echo is broken.

TLDR: Could be intentional formatting is what I want to say.

> Like somebody wants to display 6 spaces or 3 lines before their hello message

We intentionally don't want to support that. I don't know of any message system that works like that. If a single message contains whitepace in the middle, then of course we shouldn't do surgery on the message. But blank lines before/after a message are just noise.

The whitespace probably should still appear when `:messages` displays the history (whitespace *between messages*). But not in the message presentation.
So, if I am understanding this correctly, only lines containing whitespace, like `\n` must be ignored. That means for `:echo "    hello"`, the "hello" should be intended, right?

> That means for `:echo " hello"`, the "hello" should be intended, right?
